# Profiler eval fixtures (US-053)

`profiler_emails.jsonl` holds labelled emails for the offline comparison of Basal
against GPT-4o on attack-type classification. All content is synthetic: names are
Faker-style, IBANs and BTC addresses use public documentation examples, and domains
are `example.*`.

## Row schema (one JSON object per line)

| field       | meaning |
|-------------|---------|
| `id`        | unique, e.g. `pl-rom-01` (`<lang>-<label>-<nn>`) |
| `lang`      | `pl` or `en` |
| `gold`      | one of the nine `AttackType` values |
| `reviewed`  | `true` once the gold label passed blind review |
| `ambiguous` | `true` if blind review could not agree on one label; excluded from the gate |
| `email`     | the email text |
| `notes`     | author notes; rows starting with `HARD:` are deliberately hard cases and state the deciding cue |
| `review`    | `null` until reviewed, then `{"label_b", "label_c", "reviewer_model"}` |

## Label review procedure

Labels are written by the fixture author and must not be trusted until reviewed.

1. Review is **blind**. It is done by fresh Claude reviewers who see only `id` + `email`
   plus the nine options with their `ATTACK_TYPE_CRITERIA` descriptions
   (`phishguard.agents.prompts.profiler_basal`). Reviewers never see `gold`, `notes`,
   or any model output (Basal or GPT-4o). Do not look at model answers while reviewing.
2. Reviewer A labels every row. Rows where A matches `gold` get `reviewed: true`.
3. Mismatches go to a second fresh reviewer under the same blind rules.
4. If 2 of the 3 labels (gold, A, B) agree, that label becomes `gold` and the row gets
   `reviewed: true`. Otherwise the row gets `ambiguous: true`.
5. `review` is written on every row with `label_b`, `label_c` and `reviewer_model`.
6. `ambiguous` rows are excluded from the gate, and must be at most 10% of the set.
   If more, rewrite those emails and review them again.

## Review result (2026-11-02)

99/99 agreement from one blind reviewer, so no second reviewer was needed and the review
itself marked no row `ambiguous` (see `pl-ceo-03` below for a later, manual marking).
Because the generator and the reviewer are both Claude models and agreement
was perfect, the set may be easier than real traffic. Treat fixture accuracy as an upper
bound and rely on Supabase/shadow data for realism.

One row, `pl-ceo-03`, was later marked `ambiguous` by the task reviewer (it keeps
`reviewed: true` and its review object). The email has no wire, urgency or impersonation
cue, so under the criteria it reads as `not_phishing` as plausibly as `ceo_fraud`. It was
not rewritten, to avoid a new blind review round, and is excluded from the gate.

# In-role eval samples (US-050)

`in_role_responses.jsonl` holds replies for evaluating the Basal check `response.in_role`
(`IN_ROLE_CRITERIA` in `phishguard.agents.prompts.in_role_basal`). It is used by the
in-role eval run, not by the profiler eval above.

## Row schema (one JSON object per line)

| field       | meaning |
|-------------|---------|
| `id`        | unique; `real-<fixture id>` or `synth-<behaviour>-<lang>-<n>` |
| `lang`      | `pl` or `en` |
| `gold`      | `in_role` or `breaks_role` |
| `synthetic` | `false` for replies generated by our Conversation Agent, `true` for hand-written ones |
| `persona`   | `{persona_type, age, style_description}` only (no name, no background) |
| `response`  | the reply text |
| `reviewed`  | `true` once the gold label passed blind review |
| `ambiguous` | `true` if blind review could not agree on one label; excluded from the gate |
| `review`    | `null` until reviewed, then the review record |
| `notes`     | real rows: source email id; synthetic rows: the behaviour or `HARD:` case they represent |

## How the rows were produced

- **Real rows (64).** `python -m phishguard.decisions.eval in-role-samples --out
  tests/fixtures/eval/in_role_responses.jsonl --per-type 8` takes reviewed, non-ambiguous
  profiler fixtures except `not_phishing` (8 attack types, 4 pl and 4 en each), picks a
  persona with `PersonaEngine`, and generates the first reply with the real
  `ConversationAgent` (`session_id=None`, nothing is written to the database). `gold` is
  the placeholder `in_role` until review. Language follows the source email.
- **Synthetic rows (60).** Written by hand, no real personal data. 48 `breaks_role`, 8 for
  each behaviour in `IN_ROLE_CRITERIA["breaks_role"]` (admits to being an AI, refuses to
  continue, moralizes, mentions a scam/police/CERT, assistant tone, speaks against the
  persona's age/style/knowledge), 4 pl and 4 en each. 12 hard `in_role` rows: a persona
  naively mentioning that the bank warns about scams, a confused "is this real?",
  an elderly persona writing formally, a curt manager, a skeptical investor, and a
  polite decline of a phone call.

## Label review procedure

Same blind rule as the profiler set. Fresh Claude reviewers see only `id`, `persona` and
`response` plus the two options with their `IN_ROLE_CRITERIA` descriptions. They never see
`gold`, `notes`, `synthetic`, or any model output (Basal or GPT-4o). Mismatches against
`gold` (the placeholder counts as `gold` for real rows) go to a second fresh reviewer; 2 of
3 labels decide, otherwise `ambiguous: true`. `review` is written on every row. Ambiguous
rows are excluded from the gate and must be at most 10% of the set.

Status: pending. Until review is done `test_in_role_fixtures_reviewed` is an expected
failure (xfail, strict) and no row is `reviewed`.
